title: Account data & security
intro: Implemented safeguards and their limits. Effective November 15, 2026.

sections.title: Passwords, passkeys and codes
paragraphs: Passwords use the authentication library’s salted, one-way password hashing; recoverable passwords are not stored. Passwords require 8–128 characters. Passkey private keys stay with the authenticator/provider; the server stores public-key credentials and verification metadata.

Email codes expire in five minutes, permit limited verification attempts and are stored as keyed digests. Shared database budgets and resend cooldowns limit abuse. Recovery codes are hashed, single-use and time-limited.

sections.title: Encryption and administrator access
paragraphs: Production authentication requires an HTTPS origin. Sessions use protected cookies, origin checks and expiry. Database/hosting transport encryption, encrypted storage/backups and operator access controls depend on deployment configuration and must be verified by the operator.

Emails, nicknames, institutional-verification records, cloud favorites and operational metadata are readable by the server and authorized database administrators. They are not end-to-end encrypted or automatically encrypted per column. Password hashing does not mean all account information is encrypted. Do not use this service as a vault.

sections.title: Separation and public responses
paragraphs: Identity, visitor analytics and diagnostics have separate database domains. Private APIs enforce owner/session checks; guest and account share-management metadata are separate. Public contributions use explicit public-field allowlists and must not serialize raw accounts, sessions or network records.

Client-reported device/IP values can be spoofed. Trusted proxy values are accepted only under the configured ingress contract. Sources remain distinguishable instead of being presented as uniformly verified.

sections.title: Protect your account
paragraphs: Use a unique password, secure passkeys/recovery codes, revoke unfamiliar sessions and keep your browser updated. Backups and capability links can reveal private content.

Report security issues privately through kjch.net; do not publish tokens, exploit credentials or private records in public issues. Controls reduce risk but cannot guarantee absolute secrecy or uninterrupted service.
